misconceptions.description: Sending an AI-generated email without checking facts, names, dates, or tone for the real recipient
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes the AI draft and hits send, keeping a wrong professor name or invented office hours
misconceptions.feedback: Read every AI draft before sending. Verify the recipient name, dates, and any claimed facts; the AI does not know your real details.

misconceptions.description: Giving the AI a one-line prompt with no recipient, purpose, or facts, then expecting a usable email
misconceptions.trigger: learner types 'write an email to my professor' with no course, request, or deadline
misconceptions.feedback: Put the specifics in the prompt: who it is to, the course, the exact ask, and any dates. A vague prompt yields a generic, unusable draft.

misconceptions.description: Keeping an overly casual or overly stiff AI tone that does not fit a professor or employer audience
misconceptions.trigger: learner sends 'Hey can u bump my grade thx' to a professor
misconceptions.feedback: Match tone to audience. For a professor or employer, use a clear subject line, a greeting with their name, a specific request, and a sign-off.

misconceptions.description: Pasting sensitive personal data such as a student ID or grades into a public AI tool to draft an email
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes their full student ID number and medical note into the chat prompt
misconceptions.feedback: Keep private identifiers out of the prompt. Use a placeholder like [STUDENT ID] and fill it in yourself after the draft returns.
